diagnostic_evidence.quote: the set of admissible controls, denoted by $\Theta$, consists of all such control processes on $[0,1]$ that are square-integrable on $\Omega\times [0,1]$

issues.failure_explanation: The intro asserts the bridge drift $\bar\theta_t=(\xi-X_t^{0,x_0;\bar\theta})/(1-t)$, $t\in[0,1)$, is an admissible control realizing $X_1=\xi$ a.s., which 'yields the equivalence' of the unregularized problem (opt-prob) and (sto-control-prob). But by the paper's own Brownian-bridge representation (used in Lemma lem-convergence and in the proof of Theorem thm-convergence), $\mathbb E|\bar\theta_t|^2=\mathbb E|x_0-\xi|^2+d\,t/(1-t)$, hence $\int_0^1\mathbb E|\bar\theta_t|^2dt=\infty$: the un-truncated bridge control is not square-integrable and therefore is not in $\Theta$ as defined. So the attainment argument is invalid; only the equality of the infimum with $\min G$ holds, via truncated bridge controls (exactly the construction the paper later uses in Theorem thm-convergence). The claim that the optimum is attained by an element of $\Theta$ is false as written.

failure_location.quote:
Then we may take the feedback control $\bar\theta_t=\frac{\xi-X^{0,x_0;\bar\theta}_t}{1-t} \textbf{1}_{[0,1)}(t)$ and the Brownian bridge theory 
(see \cite{karatzas1998brownian}) implies that $X_1^{0,x_0;\theta}=\xi$ almost surely (a.s. for short).  This yields the equivalence of the optimization problem \eqref{opt-prob} and the stochastic control problem \eqref{sto-control-prob}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the equivalence as an equality of infima justified by the truncated Brownian-bridge controls $\tilde\theta^{\eps}$ already constructed in the proof of Theorem thm-convergence (send $\delta\to0$), and drop the claim that $\bar\theta\in\Theta$.
issues.overall_effect: The introductory claim that the unregularized control problem (sto-control-prob) is solved by an admissible control (and the resulting 'equivalence' statement) is unsupported; only an infimum-level statement, obtained via truncated controls, is justified. The later results (Theorems thm-convergence/thm-convergence-2) use truncated controls and are not affected.
issues.title: Claimed optimal Brownian-bridge feedback control is not admissible (not square-integrable), so the claimed equivalence of (opt-prob) and (sto-control-prob) is unjustified
issues.why_classification: A local, routine repair using a construction already present in the paper (truncation at $1-\delta$) preserves every substantive claim (equality of infima, all later rates and guarantees); no new argument is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the equality holds when choosing the optimal feedback control $\theta^*=-\Lions \tilde{\mathcal{V}}_{\eps}(s, \mathcal{L}(X^{t,\xi;\theta^*}_s), X^{t,\xi;\theta^*}_s)$

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed 'fundamental identity' is false as printed. From the master equation (Master-eq), the Itô–Kunita–Wentzell expansion along $dX_s=\theta_s ds+dW_s$ gives $J^\theta_\eps(t,\mu)=\tilde{\mathcal V}_\eps(t,\mu)+\mathbb E\int_t^T \tfrac{1}{2\eps}\big|\eps\theta_s+\partial_\mu\tilde{\mathcal V}_\eps\big|^2ds$ (equivalently $\tfrac{\eps}{2}|\theta_s+\eps^{-1}\partial_\mu\tilde{\mathcal V}_\eps|^2$): the factor $\eps$ belongs to $\theta$, not as printed. With the identity as printed, the cross term would be $(1/\eps)\langle\theta,\partial_\mu\tilde{\mathcal V}\rangle$ instead of $\langle\theta,\partial_\mu\tilde{\mathcal V}\rangle$. Consequently the printed equality-case control $\theta^*=-\partial_\mu\tilde{\mathcal V}_\eps$ does not annihilate the printed square (it would require $\theta^*=-\eps\,\partial_\mu\tilde{\mathcal V}_\eps$), and it contradicts the paper's own Pontryagin characterization $\theta^*_s=-\frac1\eps Y_s$ in (eq:fbsde). The verification conclusion itself survives after placing the $\eps$ correctly.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the identity by $J^\theta_\eps(t,\mu)=\tilde{\mathcal V}_\eps(t,\mu)+\mathbb E\int_t^T \tfrac{1}{2\eps}|\eps\theta_s+\partial_\mu\tilde{\mathcal V}_\eps|^2ds$ and the equality case by $\theta^*= -\eps^{-1}\Lions\tilde{\mathcal V}_\eps$ (consistent with (eq:fbsde) and the finite-dimensional verification in Theorem thm-well-posedness).
issues.overall_effect: The key displayed identity and the equality-case feedback control in the (sketch of the) proof of Lemma lem:uniqueness are wrong as written; the lemma's statement (and its later use in Proposition prop-well-posedness-mfc, Step 3) remains valid once the $\eps$ placement is corrected, since the corrected identity still yields $\tilde{\mathcal V}_\eps\le J^\theta_\eps$ with equality at the true optimal control.
issues.title: Verification identity in Lemma lem:uniqueness misplaces the factor $\eps$; stated equality-case control is wrong
issues.why_classification: A local, essentially forced correction (repositioning $\eps$ inside the square, and the matching $1/\eps$ in the feedback) restores the standard verification argument; the lemma's conclusion and every downstream use survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assuming $\mu$ has sufficiently many finite moments, Fournier and Guillin \cite{fournier2015rate} established the following rates:

issues.failure_explanation: The first branch asserts $\E\mathcal W_2(\mu^N,\mu)\le C_\alpha N^{-1/2-\alpha}$ for every $\alpha>0$ when $d\le4$, i.e., a rate faster than $N^{-1/2}$ to every polynomial order. This is false in every dimension: for any non-atomic $\mu$ the central-limit behavior of the empirical measure forces $\E\mathcal W_2\ge c\,N^{-1/2}$, so no bound of order $N^{-1/2-\alpha}$ with $\alpha>0$ can hold. What Fournier–Guillin actually give (with enough moments) is $\E\mathcal W_2\lesssim N^{-1/2}$ for $d\le 3$ (with logarithmic corrections at $d=4$), matching the paper's second branch $N^{-1/d}$ only for $d\ge5$. As printed, the sampling-error statement that qualifies Corollary cor:general_measure is mathematically false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the first branch by the actual Fournier–Guillin rates, e.g. $\E[\mathcal W_2]\le C N^{-1/2}$ for $d\le3$ (with the appropriate logarithmic correction at $d=4$), keeping the $C_2N^{-1/d}$ branch for $d\ge5$.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative description of the sampling-error term $L_G\,\E\mathcal W_2(\mu^N,\mu)$ in Corollary cor:general_measure/Remark rmk:sampling_error is materially wrong for $d\le4$; the qualitative claim that the term vanishes as $N\to\infty$ is unaffected.
issues.title: Misstated Fournier–Guillin empirical Wasserstein rates in Remark rmk:sampling_error
issues.why_classification: Correcting the quoted rates is a local edit using the cited reference; the corollary's structure and every guarantee survive with the corrected (slower) rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the corresponding Monte Carlo estimates of $\frac{1}{N} v^N_{\eps}(0, \mathbf{x})$ minus the minimum value ($=0.75$) of $G$ are plotted as a function of $1/N$
commonly referred to as the \emph{circle law} \cite{carrillo2020ellipse}

issues.failure_explanation: For the printed functional, direct computation refutes both claims. (i) Uniform measure $\mu_c$ on the unit circle: $\iint|x-y|^2d\mu_c d\mu_c=2$ (so $\iint|x-y|^2/2\,d\mu d\mu=1$) and $\iint\ln|x-y|\,d\mu_cd\mu_c=0$ (the log-energy of the unit circle is $0$), hence $G(\mu_c)=\frac12(1-0)=\frac12\neq0.75$. (ii) $\mu_c$ is not even a minimizer: for the uniform unit disk $\mu_d$, $\iint|x-y|^2/2\,d\mu_d d\mu_d=\tfrac12$ and $\iint\ln|x-y|\,d\mu_d d\mu_d=-\tfrac14$ (the disk's log-potential is $|x|^2/2-\tfrac12$ on its support), giving $G(\mu_d)=\tfrac38<\tfrac12$. The obstacle function $h(x)=\int\varphi(x-y)d\mu_d(y)$ equals $3/4$ on the support and satisfies $h(x)\ge3/4$ everywhere, so the true minimizer of the printed functional is the uniform measure on the unit disk (unique up to translation), with minimum $3/8$ — also matching the cited 'ellipse/circle law' theory, which for quadratic confinement yields a filled disk, not a measure on a circle. Thus the asserted minimizer ('unit circle'), the asserted value $0.75$, and the downstream convergence study benchmarked against 'the minimum value ($=0.75$)' are all incorrect for the functional as printed.

failure_location.quote:
For this purely interaction-driven energy, the global minimizer is not unique but known explicitly: 
it is the uniform probability measure supported on a unit circle, with minimal energy equal to $0.75$, 
commonly referred to as the \emph{circle law} \cite{carrillo2020ellipse}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the ground truth for the printed functional (minimizer: uniform measure on the unit disk, up to translation; minimum value $3/8$; more generally, for the printed normalization the minimum is $(1/2)\cdot(3/4)$), update the reference value used in Figure fig:convergence_rate and the surrounding text, and re-derive/relabel the reported 'confirmation' of the $O(1/N)$ rate accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The example's stated ground truth (minimizer and minimal energy 0.75) is false, so the reported convergence study in Figure fig:convergence_rate — value errors computed 'minus the minimum value (=0.75)' and the claim that extrapolation to $N\to\infty$ yields a vanishing asymptotic error — is calibrated to a wrong target and is unreliable. The paper's theorems are unaffected.
issues.title: 2D Newtonian Swarm example: stated minimizer and minimum value are both wrong
issues.why_classification: The fix is contained — recompute the equilibrium measure/energy for the printed functional and correct the example's stated ground truth and the benchmark value — but it is not routine: it requires actually solving the stated variational problem (circle vs. disk, value $1/2$ vs. $3/8$) and withdraws the example's advertised ground truth and the empirical extrapolation claim, while leaving all theorems intact; this fits the moderate band.
